ctx.x: City and ventured on . But Bennie Moten, I understand, had been up this way and played the Pearl Theater in Philadelphia or the 'Standard, or one of those theaters

It's a funny thing, though, Dan, that a band like Alphonso Trent whom I give an A' rating... and I guess I was influenced by the fact that it was the first, you know, organized from band that I heard. Because Trent started/like a five-piece band to go on to become, you know, a twelve-or fourteen-piece band when the conductor was Stuff Smith conducting. I never will forget that first band that I heard in front of Ella B. Moore's theater was something with A. G. Godley playing drums and Snub Mosley playing trombone…

Well, even a five or six piece band like that...playing together and playing different things and going from one key to the other, and really swinging, you know, this was unusual. And they went on and into strange things. However, as great as they were, and as great as they played together, they didn't come to New York City.
